results.title: Artificial Intelligence and Assessment: Are Universities Ready to Rethink Integrity?
results.content: As artificial intelligence continues to reshape higher education, one of the most pressing challenges facing universities is how to respond to student use of AI in assessment. In such environments, students may have fewer opportunities for in-person support or modelling of good academic practices, making it harder to spot – and even harder to prevent – unauthorised use of tools like ChatGPT or AI-enabled paraphrasing software. Instead of policing from a distance, we could reframe our institutional approach to academic integrity as a developmental journey—one where students are **explicitly educated** in the principles of ethical academic work; **enabled to practise** and refine these skills within safe, formative spaces; and then held to **high expectations** once the groundwork has been laid. By giving students structured opportunities to practice citation, paraphrasing, and critical use of sources—even experimenting with AI tools in ethical ways—we reduce the fear of “getting it wrong” and make space for authentic learning.
